title: Structs on the heap

notes: item_new allocates sizeof *it: the size of the struct, not of a pointer.
If the name can't be allocated, it frees the struct and returns NULL: no half-made items.
The item owns its name, so item_free frees the name first, then the struct.
item_free(NULL) does nothing, so cleanup works even if item_new failed.
main pairs each item_new with one item_free, the same way you pair fopen with fclose.

exercises.title: sensor_new and sensor_free
exercises.prompt: With the Sensor struct and str_copy given (both use my_alloc), write Sensor *sensor_new(const char *name, double alarm_at): allocate the struct with my_alloc, give it its own copy of name, set alarm_at, count 0 and last 0.0. Return NULL if name is NULL or memory runs out (free anything you already made). Then write void sensor_free(Sensor *s) that frees the name and the struct; it does nothing when s is NULL.

tests.call: ({ Sensor *s = sensor_new("tank 1", 80.0); static char b[64]; strcpy(b, s->name); sensor_free(s); b; })
tests.name: stores the name

tests.call: ({ Sensor *s = sensor_new("soil", 35.5); double r = s->alarm_at + s->count + s->last; sensor_free(s); r; })
tests.name: every field set

tests.call: ({ char nm[] = "pump"; Sensor *s = sensor_new(nm, 1.0); nm[0] = 'd'; static char b[64]; strcpy(b, s->name); sensor_free(s); b; })
tests.name: its own copy of the name
tests.hint_if_fail: Use str_copy(name), don't just store the pointer.

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; Sensor *s = sensor_new("a", 1.0); int during = live_allocs - before; sensor_free(s); during * 10 + (live_allocs - before); })
tests.name: two blocks made, both freed
tests.hint_if_fail: sensor_free must free s->name and then s.

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; Sensor *s = sensor_new(NULL, 1.0); sensor_free(NULL); (s == NULL) * 10 + (live_allocs - before); })
tests.name: NULL name and sensor_free(NULL)

hints: If s->name is NULL: my_free(s); return NULL;
sensor_free: if (s == NULL) return; my_free(s->name); my_free(s);

exercises.title: Clinic stock list
exercises.prompt: With the Medicine struct given, write Medicine *stock_new(int n): ONE my_alloc block holding n medicines, every one set to an empty name, stock 0 and min_stock 0 (NULL if n is 0 or negative). Then write int count_low(const Medicine *m, int n): how many medicines have stock below min_stock (equal is not low).

tests.call: ({ Medicine *m = stock_new(3); m[0].stock = 2; m[0].min_stock = 10; m[1].stock = 50; m[1].min_stock = 20; m[2].stock = 5; m[2].min_stock = 5; int r = count_low(m, 3); my_free(m); r; })
tests.name: one is low

tests.call: ({ Medicine *m = stock_new(4); int r = (m[3].name[0] == 0) + m[3].stock + m[3].min_stock; strcpy(m[3].name, "zinc"); my_free(m); r; })
tests.name: starts empty
tests.hint_if_fail: my_alloc doesn't clear memory: set every field (memset or a loop).

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; Medicine *m = stock_new(5); int r = (live_allocs - before) * 100 + (int)(last_alloc_size / sizeof(Medicine)); my_free(m); r; })
tests.name: one block of n medicines

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; Medicine *m = stock_new(0); (m == NULL) * 10 + (live_allocs - before); })
tests.name: n of 0: NULL

tests.call: ({ Medicine *m = stock_new(2); m[0].min_stock = 1; m[1].min_stock = 1; int r = count_low(m, 2) * 10 + count_low(m, 0); my_free(m); r; })
tests.name: all low, and an empty list

hints: memset(m, 0, n * sizeof *m); makes every name empty and every number 0.

exercises.title: Spawn and despawn
exercises.prompt: A game world has MAX_ENEMIES slots, each pointing at a heap Enemy or NULL; world_free is given. Write int spawn(World *w, const char *kind, int hp): find the first NULL slot, my_alloc an Enemy there, copy kind into it (at most 15 letters, always ending with '\0'), set hp, and return the slot number. Return -1 if every slot is taken or memory runs out. Then write int clear_dead(World *w): free every enemy whose hp is 0 or less, set its slot to NULL, and return how many were freed.

tests.call: ({ World w = {0}; int a = spawn(&w, "slime", 5); int b = spawn(&w, "bat", 3); world_free(&w); a * 10 + b; })
tests.name: slots 0 then 1

tests.call: ({ World w = {0}; spawn(&w, "wolf", 12); static char b[16]; strcpy(b, w.slots[0]->kind); world_free(&w); b; })
tests.name: copies the kind

tests.call: ({ int before = live_allocs; World w = {0}; spawn(&w, "a", 5); spawn(&w, "b", 5); spawn(&w, "c", 5); w.slots[0]->hp = 0; w.slots[2]->hp = -3; int n = clear_dead(&w); int r = n * 100 + (w.slots[0] == NULL) * 10 + (live_allocs - before); world_free(&w); r; })
tests.name: clears the dead
tests.hint_if_fail: Free each dead enemy and set its slot to NULL.

tests.call: ({ World w = {0}; for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) spawn(&w, "bat", 1); int r = spawn(&w, "bat", 1); world_free(&w); r; })
tests.name: full world

tests.call: ({ World w = {0}; spawn(&w, "a", 5); spawn(&w, "b", 5); w.slots[0]->hp = 0; clear_dead(&w); int r = spawn(&w, "c", 5); world_free(&w); r; })
tests.name: reuses a freed slot

tests.call: ({ World w = {0}; spawn(&w, "ancient_fire_dragon_lord", 100); int r = (int)strlen(w.slots[0]->kind); world_free(&w); r; })
tests.name: long names are cut to 15 letters

hints: Loop over the slots; the first w->slots[i] == NULL is where the enemy goes.
Enemy *e = my_alloc(sizeof *e); strncpy(e->kind, kind, sizeof e->kind - 1); e->kind[sizeof e->kind - 1] = '\0';
clear_dead: if (w->slots[i] != NULL && w->slots[i]->hp <= 0) { my_free(w->slots[i]); w->slots[i] = NULL; n++; }

quiz.q: Why does sensor_free free s->name before s?
choices: Once s is freed you can't safely read s->name to free it
free only works on strings first
quiz.why: Inside things first, then the container.

choices: It allocates the size of a pointer, not of the struct
quiz.why: Use sizeof *s so the size always matches.

quiz.q: sensor_new's struct allocation works but copying the name fails. What should it do?
choices: Free the struct and return NULL
quiz.why: The caller should get a whole sensor or NULL.

quiz.q: Enemies spawn and die one at a time during a level. Which fits best?
choices: One block that you realloc for every death
An array of pointers, each NULL or pointing at its own enemy
A fixed local array inside spawn
quiz.why: Free one enemy and mark its slot NULL.

quiz.q: Which pair from the standard library follows the same create/destroy pattern?
quiz.why: fopen makes a FILE, fclose destroys it.

cards.q: Create/destroy pair for a type T?
cards.a: T *t_new(...) returns a ready struct or NULL; void t_free(T *t) frees everything it owns, safe on NULL.

cards.q: Freeing order for a struct that owns memory?
cards.a: Fields it owns first, then the struct.

cards.q: After freeing a slot in an array of pointers?

explain: Explain what it means for a struct to own memory, using a struct you invent (a patient, a robot part, a game item).
